machine.topology: inner rotor, squirrel cage with closed pear-shaped slots, semi-closed trapezoidal stator slots with wedges
machine.symmetry: Full cross-section, as the paper's model; A = 0 on the stator's outer circle. Magnetostatic, nonlinear, instantaneous currents at t = 0.

components_map.part: stator: 48 semi-closed slots (opening, 45-degree wedge, trapezoidal conductive part, flat bottom), parallel teeth
line between each slot's wedge and its conductive part
single-layer winding: 48 slot circuits of 14 conductors, currents of eq. (1) at t = 0
rotor: 38 closed pear-shaped bar slots with a neck under a bridge, each bar a circuit (eq. (26))
air gap split by a mid-gap circle, shaft, outer boundary

gaps.item: slot geometry (stator opening, wedge, slot body; rotor slot shape, bridge, neck; shaft)
gaps.note: The 2023 companion paper is not cached (downloads need approval); Fig. 1 and Fig. 5 are renderings of the author's FEMM model, read by pooling all slots' outlines (0.45 mm pixels; pooled edges within about 0.1 mm, both figures agree within 0.1 mm). The rotor bridge (0.45 mm) and neck (1.5 mm) are at the resolution limit: controls bridge-0p25 and bridge-0p65.

gaps.affects: every SIM and load flux (yokes, rotor core), a few percent
gaps.note: Table 1 gives GOST's five reference points from 1.54 T; the paper says it uses this main curve. The model gives FEMM exactly those points (FEMM adds the origin), as the paper describes; control bh-low-field substitutes a typical lamination's low-field shape.
Core steel (flux lines cross the shaft in Figs. 1 and 5); control shaft-air.

gaps.affects: the torque's sign and gamma_psi1's sign
gaps.note: Eq. (26) with alpha_sr = -82.49 (p. 10, and Fig. 8's arrow) and the text's later +83.10 and +83.41 disagree, and the text's gamma_psi1 = -56.55 disagrees with Fig. 3's curve. The model's stator teeth and one rotor slot sit on the y axis, so changing alpha_sr's sign is a mirror image with every current reversed: flux, flux linkage amplitudes, EMFs and |torque| are unchanged, the torque and the phase change sign. Magnitudes are the acceptance quantities; the step load1_mirror and the torque_mirror relation check the symmetry, and control final-angle-positive uses the printed sign.

gaps.item: where the flux points Az1, Az2 lie
gaps.note: Fig. 1 marks them on the air gap: A's extremes on the circle in the middle of the gap; comparators 0.05 mm from either side.

As printed eq. (4) is twice the standard N la (A1 - A2) per turn; the paper's numbers follow the standard one (Es = 218.7 V from 0.9843 Wb; Ns kw Phi0 = 0.972 Wb). The model sums 14 conductors per slot.

gaps.item: the intermediate load point (Imu = 7.25 A, Is = 29.22 A)
gaps.affects: its torque 95.45 N m and psi_m1 0.9101 Wb
gaps.note: Its bar current is not printed, and the equivalent-circuit formulas do not reproduce the first point's printed currents exactly (Ir 448-450 A against 446 A), so it is not derived.

gaps.note: The paper's alternative with separate curves for teeth and backs needs teeth/back regions and full curves the paper does not give.

Magnetic-circuit estimate with the frozen inputs (estimate.py, Kopylov's procedure, Carter factor 1.22, the main curve through the origin): Phi0 = 9.063 mWb needs Imu = 7.4-8.6 A for calculated pole-arc coefficients 0.72-0.69 (tooth flux densities 1.68-1.75 T stator, 1.57-1.64 T rotor; yoke 1.61 T), against the paper's 7.75 A: the model should land within a few percent of the paper's flux. Torque: 3/2 p psi_m1 I_s,peak sin(56.55 deg) with the paper's own psi_m1 = 0.9313 Wb gives 94.9 N m against 97.72 (P_em/Omega_s).

Gap layers and openings 27k (0.2 mm), wedges 5k, stator conductors 19k, stator iron 52k, rotor iron 39k, bars 16k, shaft 1k, plus refinement at the bridges and corners; mesh-0p75 about 1.8 times. Two solves per FEMM process keep the container well under 2 GB (320k x 360 B x 2 = 0.23 GB of growth for the mesh control).
